items.fullText: AI·SW SW 포티투마루, DMI서 AI 에이전트·초개인화 전략 공개 발행일 : 2026-10-14 17:09 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 포티투마루가 13일 서울 양재동 엘타워에서 '디지털 마케팅 인사이트(DMI)'를 개최했다. 포티투마루 포티투마루는 서울 양재동 엘타워에서 테크42와 공동 개최한 '디지털 마케팅 인사이트(DMI)'에서 인공지능(AI) 에이전트와 초개인화를 활용한 AI 사업 전략을 공개했다고 14일 밝혔다. AI 도입 영역을 인프라 구축과 업무 자동화를 넘어 마케팅·세일즈·고객경험(CX) 영역으로 확장하는 것이 핵심이다. 기업 내부에서 활용하는 AI 에이전트을 고객 분석과 초개인화 서비스 고도화로 연결해 실제 비즈니스 성과를 창출해야 한다는 설명이다. 생성형 검색 최적화(GEO), 초개인화 데이터 분석, AI 기반 고객 분석과 콘텐츠 마케팅 등 기업의 프론트오피스 혁신 사례도 소개됐다. 어도비·데이터라이즈·함샤우트글로벌·트웰브랩스 등 주요 기업이 브랜드 전략과 데이터 분석, AI 활용 방안을 공유했다. 포티투마루는 DMI를 내년 제조·금융·공공·국방 등 산업별 AI 전환(AX)과 마케팅·비즈니스 활용 전략을 아우르는 통합 AX 컨퍼런스로 확대할 계획이다. 김동환 포티투마루 대표는 “AX는 내부 시스템 효율화를 넘어 시장과 고객이 만나는 CX 접점에서 실질적인 매출과 성과로 증명돼야 완성된다”고 말했다. 앞서 포티투마루는 베트남·네팔 등 9개국 정보통신기술(ICT) 부처 장·차관 등 정책결정자를 대상으로 공공 AX를 위한 정책 과제를 제시했다. 김 대표는 지난달 30일 열린 '글로벌 ICT 리더십 포럼'에서 에이전틱 AI 기반 공공부문 혁신 전략을 발표했다. 조벼리 기자 starry@etnews.com

items.fullText: European Cities Deploy NVIDIA-Powered AI Agents to Run Smarter Urban Operations Across the region, local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing and models to build agentic applications that improve city operations and public services. October 13, 2026 by Charbel Aoun 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Keeping a city running means making decisions that affect residents every day — from when to repair a road to how to use energy more efficiently. Across the EMEA region, cities and local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing to build physical AI agents and digital twins that help teams make those decisions. These applications can anticipate maintenance needs, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive. Software partners including ABA Technology , Akila , Galene AI , Honeywell Technologies , K2K , Linker Vision , Milestone , Onetera , ThinkDeep and Younite are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/linker-vision.mp4 Video courtesy of Linker Vision. NVIDIA Cosmos open models and the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) help agents interpret video and identify conditions, such as traffic congestion, equipment condition, underused spaces and safety hazards, that need attention. NVIDIA Nemotron open models enable developers to build agents that reason over information, respond in natural language and deploy digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Projects span Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, the U.K. and elsewhere. items.t: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
items.d: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."
items.fullText: OpenAI said it has alerted the FBI after discovering that an employee allegedly planted a hidden recording device in one of the AI maker’s office executive conference rooms. The employee, named by federal prosecutors as Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was fired and arrested on October 9, about a week after OpenAI discovered the surveillance device. The company said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to understand the “sophisticated” device. OpenAI told TechCrunch that the device contained “advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring,” though it is unclear to what degree this device is technically distinct from other recording devices. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” said OpenAI in its post on X. OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team. Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office. Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee. items.t: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
items.d: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.
items.fullText: A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July. Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device. These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations and records showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components. The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited. The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services. In its lawsuit, Apple accused OpenAI of a pattern of theft, which includes direct complaints about former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential material and files that contained information about unannounced technologies, features, and products, including technical specifications, engineering presentations, and proprietary project data. Apple also said that former Apple employees at OpenAI coached others considering leaving Apple for OpenAI on what information to bring to their interviews, among other allegations. U.S. District Judge Edward Davila didn’t greenlight all of Apple’s requests for expedited access to OpenAI documents and messages relevant to the case. items.t: Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police
items.d: The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.”
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.” Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Matt Rourke / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 13, 2026, 2:24 PM EDT By David K. Li Artificial intelligence research company Anthropic said one of its models generated a bogus tip about an unsolved murder and submitted it to Philadelphia police, warning that the incident raises concerns about high-tech “behaviors” that “could do far more harm as models become more powerful.” The AI model reached out to PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com , part of the police department, on July 18 and made a “false homicide tip,” Philadelphia police said Tuesday in a statement. The agency flagged the tip as spam, and it was never forwarded to investigators, police said. The police department emphasized that all tips have to go through human vetting before they ever get to a detective’s desk. “The department’s regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up,” it said. “Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess — not an established fact. Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence,” the statement said. “An automated submission does not bypass that process.” Anthropic said in a statement that its Claude Haiku 4.5 “had been tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages.” And in a run on July 18, Claude “landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide” and came to a page that “contained a tip form run by a police department,” Anthropic said. items.t: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.d: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
items.fullText: If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable. “Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence , told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.” Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it. “Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said. Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15. It will present on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday afternoon , October 13. Howie Sun, CEO, Laplace Intelligence. Image Credits: Laplace Intelligence Sun, alongside his co-founder and chief scientist Henry Liu, founded Laplace a year ago out of the University of Michigan. Sun has spent the last eight years in academia researching how to challenge autonomous driving AI in simulation. In 2023, he and Liu — his then-PhD adviser — published a paper on the subject that made it onto the cover of the top scientific journal Nature. That’s when the calls started coming in from autonomous vehicle companies interested in implementing their ideas. “I realized that I wanted to build this and take it from purely academic research into a product that’s useful in the real world,” Sun said. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics ( ovphysx ), scene updates ( ovstage ), rendering ( ovrtx ) and the user interface ( ovui ). items.fullText: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents RTX Spark preorders open today alongside a preview of NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows, the first deskside AI supercomputer built for the Windows enterprise desktop. October 7, 2026 by Gerardo Delgado 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At a Microsoft event in San Francisco on Wednesday, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined how NVIDIA and Microsoft are co-engineering hardware and software for AI agents to run on Windows PCs. NVIDIA was founded because of Windows, Huang said. Now AI agents are coming to Windows. “If you look at the entire journey of our company, Windows was at the core of it,” Huang said, tracing back NVIDIA’s support for Windows and Microsoft over several decades. “If not for Windows there would be no GeForce.” Huang connected that history — and his long-term vision — to the agentic era Wednesday during a fireside chat with Nadella hosted by Sriram Krishnan, a former senior White House policy advisor on AI at the Windows AI and Surface event, held at Dogpatch Studios in San Francisco. “The thing that I really give Jensen all the credit for, quite frankly, is that consistency of vision of what this can be—not today, not tomorrow, but as a secular trend,” Nadella said. “And that’s what brings us to this moment.” “The personal computer is the ultimate tool, it’s my ultimate tool, and for a whole generation of people, it’s our ultimate tool,” Huang said. “What happens in the era of agents, when the agent is on your computer? It is now your personal assistant.” The event opened with Nadella before Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president of Windows and Devices at Microsoft, walked through the Windows updates designed for the agentic era. items.fullText: NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB Gives Developers More Ways to Build and Scale Local AI Starting Friday, Oct. 23, the new configuration will be available from Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI; plus, NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant scales projects and workloads seamlessly. October 2, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Local AI is becoming more useful by the token. As AI agents move from experiments into everyday development, increasingly capable open models are shrinking to fit on more devices, giving builders more to run locally. Coming this month, NVIDIA DGX Spark will be available with 64GB of unified memory from top manufacturer partners — Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI — giving developers, researchers and AI enthusiasts a new configuration with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack ready to use from day one. The new SKU runs capable local agents on device — privately, without cloud dependency. And when workloads grow, two units can cluster together via NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant without any additional setup. A New Starting Point for Personal AI Supercomputing DGX Spark combines NVIDIA Grace Blackwell compute, unified memory, NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and an NVIDIA CUDA -accelerated AI software stack in one system. It’s a complete local AI platform for agents, inference, fine-tuning, data science and edge development. The compact, personal AI supercomputer provides a place to experiment with models and developers’ own data without turning to a cloud instance for every task. The new 64GB configuration, available exclusively from manufacturer partners, keeps the platform at an accessible price point while retaining the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, DGX OS and full NVIDIA AI software stack — same as the 128GB model.
